stem: A worker repeatedly develops eye and breathing irritation during dusty plant handling. What is the most appropriate response?
choices: Assume the symptoms are unrelated to work unless they also occur away from the facility.
Continue the task with added PPE and report the symptoms only if they become more severe.
Report the recurring work-related eye and breathing symptoms and follow the workplace health/safety process so exposure and controls can be evaluated.
Switch to a different task informally and avoid the dusty area without creating a health/safety record.
rationale: Repeated eye or breathing irritation associated with dusty plant handling may indicate a work-related exposure or sensitization concern. Reporting the pattern allows the workplace to evaluate exposure, controls, and medical follow-up as appropriate. Quietly changing tasks or waiting for severe symptoms can leave the underlying hazard unaddressed for both the worker and others performing the same work.
